intent: Give explicit interactive native encounters a bounded queue advantage and release shared GPU turns atomically.

changed_behavior.interactive: Only JSON boolean true scopes interactive intent; nested calls and exceptions restore previous scope.
changed_behavior.queue: Interactive tickets use a 500ms virtual arrival head start. Real timeout clocks remain unchanged. Ordinary tickets age ahead of later arrivals; this is not a wall-time guarantee.
changed_behavior.prefill: Interactive groups carry 32 layers; background groups carry 8. Wide token matmuls and model/KV ownership remain intact.
changed_behavior.release: The owned directory is atomically renamed before cleanup so a new holder's path cannot turn a completed release into a reported failure.

live_observations.workload: Three overlapping native jobs; peers still use whole-slice code
After third job exited; one whole-slice background peer remains

limits: These two measurements have different host loads; they do not isolate the queue-policy effect.
Shared responsiveness still requires active peers to adopt the bounded prefill code.
A longer interactive group can delay another interactive request; no mid-group preemption is claimed.
No prefix cache or permanent resident companion is claimed.

observed_failure.kind: gpu lease release returned rmdir-failed after shared execution
observed_failure.cause: Host recursive removal checks path existence after removal; another waiter can recreate the public path before that check.
observed_failure.repair_proof: Deterministic interleaving recreates a new lease during cleanup and verifies it survives unchanged.

privacy: Only aggregate measurements are public; private encounter input and response stay local.

sovereignty.implementation_and_review: OpenAI gpt-6-astra; task-specific token counts unavailable

lesson: Fair turn ordering alone does not ensure responsiveness: turn cost, live adoption, host load, and atomic ownership handoff are separate observations.
